one_liner: Hand-written Armv8-A Neon assembly NTTs for Kyber, Dilithium and Saber; about 4-6x faster than reference-C Dilithium NTTs.
what_it_does: Artifact of the TCHES 2022 paper 'Neon NTT: Faster Dilithium, Kyber, and Saber on Cortex-A72 and Apple M1'. Each scheme directory (kyber512/768/1024, lightsaber/saber/firesaber, dilithium2/3/5) holds the polynomial arithmetic in .S files (__asm_NTT.S, __asm_iNTT.S, __asm_base_mul.S or __asm_mul.S, __asm_poly.S), a full scheme ready to drop into SUPERCOP or PQClean behind the NIST crypto_kem_*/crypto_sign_* API, a Cortex-A72 microbenchmark and an Apple M1 benchmark. It is a source tree to copy from, not a packaged library.
how_it_is_fast: The paper's core idea is 'Barrett multiplication', a Montgomery/Barrett hybrid for multiplying by a known constant with Neon sqrdmulh/mul/mls, combined with two-unknown-factor Montgomery multiplication, Barrett reduction sequences and interleaved multi-stage butterflies that merge NTT layers to cut loads and stores. 'Asymmetric multiplication' caches precomputed products of the incomplete NTT so matrix-vector products do less work, and Saber switches from Toom-Cook or 16-bit NTTs plus CRT to a single 32-bit NTT. Full-scheme numbers also use a two-way Neon Keccak on Cortex-A72 and Keccak with the M1's SHA-3 instructions (feat.S from armed-keccak).
when_to_use: Round-3 Kyber or Dilithium on 64-bit Armv8-A application cores (Cortex-A72 class, Apple M1) where polynomial arithmetic dominates: dilithium3 signing 2.12x the reference on Cortex-A72 and 3.3x on M1 (derived from paper Table 6).
Matrix-vector-heavy lattice code: kyber768 MatrixVectorMul 11 077 cycles on Cortex-A72 and 2 291 on M1; dilithium2 26 268 vs 135 182 cycles for reference C.

As a reference design when porting Neon NTTs to another lattice scheme or modulus; the Barrett-multiplication and asymmetric-multiplication tricks are documented in the paper and visible in the .S files.
Reproducible academic baseline: pinned commit a96c17d plus SUPERCOP 20210604 reproduce the paper's full-scheme tables on a Raspberry Pi 4.
when_not_to_use: Production ML-KEM/ML-DSA (FIPS 203/204): the paper code is round-3 Kyber/Dilithium; HEAD's Oct 2024 commits ('update dilithium to standard', 'sync to standard') move toward the standards, but the README documents no conformance testing. The maintained route is mlkem-native (SLOTHY-scheduled AArch64 assembly with HOL-Light proofs, default in liboqs 0.13.0 and in AWS-LC).
Anything other than 64-bit Arm: no x86 path, and a 32-bit OS fails with assembler errors such as "bad instruction 'stp x19,x20,...'" (issue #1); for Cortex-M4 use pqm4, for RISC-V use PQRV.
Saber at HEAD: commit fb2e067 (2024-10-12) says 'Saber not working now, but will soon' and no later commit message reports a fix; Saber was also not standardised by NIST.
When you already have a good Neon Kyber: against Nguyen-Gaj's Neon code full Kyber is only 9-14% faster on Cortex-A72.
When you need documented side-channel review or formal verification: neither is claimed in the README or the paper's results section.

integration.dependencies: none for the kernels; full schemes need a randombytes source (SUPERCOP's, or the bundled one in m1_benchmarks) and use the bundled fips202/fips202x2 Keccak; M1 benchmarks need m1cycles.c and root
integration.min_toolchain: gcc 10.3.0 on 64-bit Ubuntu 21.04 (tested) or Apple clang 12.0.5 on macOS 11.4 (tested); any aarch64 assembler with Neon
integration.platforms: aarch64 (Armv8-A Neon) only; tested on Cortex-A72 (Raspberry Pi 4) and Apple M1; the M1 Keccak path needs the SHA-3 extension; benchmark harness tested only on Cortex-A72
integration.thread_safety: not documented (the kernels read caller buffers and constant tables; no global state seen in the files read)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: a scheme directory replaces the round-3 reference implementation behind the same crypto_kem_*/crypto_sign_* API, but only on aarch64 and only for the round-3 parameter sets

gotchas: Cross-run comparisons behind the Kyber/Saber headlines: Table 5's Cortex-A72 Nguyen-Gaj rows are round hundreds (kyber768 MatrixVectorMul 19 300, saber 71 300) and Table 6's Apple M1 Nguyen-Gaj rows (23 000, 36 300, 51 300) carry no 're-benchmarked in SUPERCOP' footnote, unlike the Cortex-A72 full-scheme rows; so the abstract's 1.7x/2.1x kyber768 MatrixVectorMul and the 26-41% M1 full-Kyber gains appear to compare fresh runs against figures from the earlier paper. Only the Cortex-A72 full-scheme rows are same-harness.

Prior work has moved: Nguyen-Gaj's PQC_NEON README now lists Kyber NTT 1,162 and inverse NTT 1,320 cycles and Kyber512 keypair 68,919 on Cortex-A72, against 1 200 / 1 338 / 62 459 here (the paper notes Nguyen-Gaj counts omit a final reduction), so the remaining lead is in matrix-vector multiplication, not the bare NTT.

Harness details: the M1 harness averages one counter pair around 1 000 000-iteration loops, signs 32-byte messages (MLEN 32) where the paper says 59-byte, and adds polyveck_reduce to its MatrixVectorMul timing, which the Cortex-A72 speed.c does not; both harnesses time kernels on uninitialised stack arrays (harmless for constant-time kernels). Full-scheme Dilithium gains also mix in faster Keccak (Neon two-way on A72, SHA-3 instructions on M1) against reference fips202.c, and the paper does not separate the two.

HEAD is not the measured code: 2024 commits switched Kyber to 16-bit subtractive Montgomery and Barrett variants, rewrote constants and macros and added PQClean namespacing; reproduce from a96c17d (which already contains the x29 frame-pointer fix from PQClean issue #431). Cortex-A72 cycle counting needs the bundled enable_ccr kernel module ('Illegal instruction' otherwise), and the M1 counters need sudo.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick neon-ntt over pqm4 (Cortex-M4) and PQRV (RISC-V) when the target is a 64-bit Armv8-A core with Neon; for maintained FIPS 203 code on AArch64, mlkem-native (not catalogued) builds on the same line of work.
verified_claims_summary: On a Raspberry Pi 4 (Cortex-A72 at 1.5 GHz, gcc 10.3.0 -O3, PMU medians) and an Apple M1 (Apple clang 12.0.5 -O3, averages), the dilithium3 Neon NTT takes 2 241 cycles against 9 302 for pq-crystals reference C (4.15x; 5.98x on M1), dilithium2 MatrixVectorMul 26 268 against 135 182 (5.15x), and full dilithium3 signing in SUPERCOP 20210604 1 089 387 against 2 308 598 cycles (2.12x). Against Nguyen-Gaj's Neon Kyber, full Kyber is 9-14% faster in a same-harness SUPERCOP re-run on Cortex-A72 (ratios derived from paper data).
status_note: Stale research artifact (last commit 2024-11-10, 34 stars, all 5 issues closed), MIT or CC0 and easy to vendor per scheme; reproduce from commit a96c17d, treat the Kyber/Saber-versus-Nguyen-Gaj MatrixVectorMul and M1 full-scheme gains as cross-paper comparisons, and prefer a maintained FIPS 203/204 implementation in production.
